# libjxl / icc_codec_fuzzer

libjxl's own fuzz target `icc_codec_fuzzer` ([source](source/icc_codec_fuzzer.cc), unmodified), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over libjxl (libjxl/libjxl at aea3a06e).

Checks 4 properties (listed below); the first, a round trip: For every input whose first byte is non-zero: UnpredictICC(PredictICC(x)) reproduces x exactly (same size and memcmp equal) -- the ICC predictive codec is lossless on ARBITRARY bytes, not only on valid profiles.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against libjxl at commit aea3a06e.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- PredictICC (the writer) must succeed on every byte string ("Writing should support any random bytestream so must succeed") ([line 93](source/icc_codec_fuzzer.cc#L93)): a trap; confirmed in the binary.
- For every input whose first byte is non-zero: UnpredictICC(PredictICC(x)) reproduces x exactly (same size and memcmp equal) -- the ICC predictive codec is lossless on ARBITRARY bytes, not only on valid profiles ([line 95](source/icc_codec_fuzzer.cc#L95)): a trap; confirmed in the binary.
- Every allocation the library made through the harness TrackingMemoryManager was freed by the end of the run (num_allocations==0, allocation map empty, bytes_in_use==0): a leak check on the JxlMemoryManager path that holds without LeakSanitizer ([line 101](source/icc_codec_fuzzer.cc#L101)): a trap; confirmed in the binary.

A failed check marked as ending the process contradicts every halts statement below, so a proof of one implies them on every input it covers.
